taxonomyNote: NatureServe: formerly L. leucomelana; Sibley and Monroe (1990) argued the original spelling leucomelana is correct.
fieldMarks: About 33 in (84 cm) long; males black with a grey belly, females mottled brown
Bare red skin patch around the eyes and a crest of feathers atop the head
behavior: Relatively common in upland areas; often seen scurrying by
habitat: Relatively common in Hawaiʻi Island's upland areas; Hawaiʻi Birding Trails lists it at wet-forest, dry-forest and pasture-and-grassland sites.
range: Native to southern Asia; first brought to Hawaii in 1962 as a gamebird. NatureServe records it in Hawaii.
